# Guide to the supporting code {#sec-app-code}

Every numerical or symbolic claim in this book that is not a textbook result is backed by a script in the repository [github.com/gustavdelius/affine_toda](https://github.com/gustavdelius/affine_toda). The scripts are Python 3 with numpy, scipy, sympy and mpmath (`requirements.txt`), and all of them are in the directory `textbook_code/`. Wherever the text names a script, the name links to its source.

The scripts directly in `textbook_code/` run on their own and print one `PASS` or `FAIL` line per check. They cover the textbook material, Parts VII and VIII, appendix A and parts of Part IX. The larger computations are in subdirectories. Each of their scripts is run from its own directory, and most print tables or residuals, with the stored output next to them.

| Subdirectory | Parts | What it contains |
|---|---|---|
| `hirota/`, `oneloop/`, `thimbles/` | V | Hirota fluctuations, transmission factors and Jordan types; one-loop masses of all folded solitons; the thimble decomposition of the reduced model and topological charges |
| `rmatrix/` | VI, appendix B | Construction of representations and R-matrices of quantum affine algebras from their defining relations, scalar factors, fusion, pole scans and breather tests for $c_n^{(1)}$, $a_{2n-1}^{(2)}$, $e_6^{(2)}$, $f_4^{(1)}$, $g_2^{(1)}$ and $d_4^{(3)}$, and the one-loop comparisons with the Toda Lagrangian |
| `vernier/`, `irf/`, `sectors/` | VI, IX | The lattice model of Vernier, Jacobsen and Saleur; RSOS face weights of $a_2^{(1)}$; Krein unitarity and the classification of multi-soliton sectors |
| `review614/` | IX | Random tests of the continuum-limit lemmas |
| `figures/` | all | Scripts that draw the figures and check the formulas they plot |

`textbook_code/README.md` describes every script, with the ids of the statements it checks. @sec-app-code-defects lists the scripts of Part VIII one by one.

## Part VIII: defects {#sec-app-code-defects}

The checks of Part VIII are in `textbook_code/` and share the helper `defect_common.py`, whose module docstring states the conventions of the part: the fields $\vec\phi$ on $x<0$ and $\vec\psi$ on $x>0$, the matrices $\mathsf D$ and $E$ of both types, the defect potential, $\sigma=e^{-\theta_d}$, the Weyl and Fock modules and the $a_r^{(1)}$ transmission matrices. Each script prints `PASS`/`FAIL` lines; the runtimes are approximate and depend on the load of the machine.

| Script | Chapters | Checks | Runtime | What it checks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `defect_axioms.py` | 36 | 20 | 3 s | the three forms of the triangle relation, the no-go reductions, the Ising and Lee–Yang defects, the doubling trick, twist defects, the Copetti–Córdova–Komatsu crossing rules |
| `defect_classical_sg.py` | 36–37 | 27 | 20 s | the Bäcklund transformation and Bianchi permutability, the sine-Gordon defect conditions and potential, soliton delays, absorption and emission, linear transmission, fusion onto a Dirichlet boundary |
| `defect_sg_transmission.py` | 37, 40 | 24 | 100–160 s | the sine-Gordon transmission matrix and its scalar factor: unitarity, crossing and the sign of $q$, the resonance, the odd sector, breather transmission, the semiclassical limit |
| `defect_classical_an.py` | 38 | 24 | 60–115 s | the momentum scan over affine diagrams, the $a_r^{(1)}$ defect conditions and potential, the defect Lax matrix, the delays, both spin-two charges, type-II defects |
| `defect_spin_two_a3.py` | 38 | 9 | about 3 min | both spin-$\pm2$ charges of $a_3^{(1)}$, exactly, $\sigma$ symbolic, both types (the $a_2$ construction generalized to a general-$r$ exact root-data basis), with controls |
| `defect_lax_rmatrix.py` | 38 | 6 | 2 s | the Dirac bracket of the defect values and the classical r-matrix bracket of $L_d$ |
| `defect_solitons_an.py` | 39 | 9 | 10 s | $a_r^{(1)}$ delays for every species, type and jump class, the stored charge and the selection rule, absorption, multi-soliton passage, linear transmission, the frozen soliton |
| `defect_universal_r.py` | 40 | 16 | 50–95 s | q-oscillator, Weyl and Fock modules, the universal R-matrix on them, uniqueness of the intertwiners, the two Borel subalgebras |
| `defect_transfer.py` | 40 | 9 | 15–35 s | Fock and Weyl traces, commutation with the transfer matrices, the TQ relations, the twist and charge-conjugation limits |
| `defect_an_transmission.py` | 41 | 28 | about 200 s | the $a_r^{(1)}$ and $a_2^{(2)}$ transmission matrices: uniqueness, triangle relation, crossing and the sign of $q$, scalar factors, poles and unstable windows, the semiclassical limit |
| `defect_doubling.py` | 42 | 20 | 15–60 s | the doubled theory, diagonal coideals, the refutation of @cnj-twisted-diagonal (least squares and the exact obstruction), the two Borel symmetries and the limits $\theta_d\to\pm\infty$, defect–boundary fusion and Corrigan and Zambon's (2.17)–(2.19), the classical dressing, tensor K-matrices |
| `defect_particle_transmission.py` | 43 | 11 | about 1 min | lightest-breather transmission for $a_2^{(1)}$–$a_4^{(1)}$, the particle transmission factors and their bootstrap, the one-loop sinh-Gordon factor, the doubled $a_r^{(1)}$ boundary and its second module, the soliton CDD condition, residue ranks of the spectrum table, the real-coupling defect vacuum |
